Doomsday was initially conceived at a meeting of a number of freelance artists and writers working on SUPERMAN in 1991 or 1992. DC recognized four of the attendees at this meeting Dan Jurgens, Jerry Ordway, Louise Simonson and Roger Stern as the co-creators of Doomsday. Jerry Ordway assigned half of his equity share to a fifth contributor, Brett Breeding, and DC recognized Breeding as a co-creator of Doomsday as well. DC has “continuity agreements” with all five of these contributors covering the time period of their creation of Doomsday. We also have character equity agreements with 4 of the 5 contributors as well as the assignment from Ordway to Breeding. Included in the COT are continuity agreements with other talent, John Bogdanove and Dennis Janke, because they contributed to the comic book issue(s) in which Doomsday first appeared. Doomsday first appeared unnamed in artwork on the last page of Superman: Man of Steel #17. Doomsday made his first appearance, by name, in Superman: The Man of Steel #18.

column12: From Benjamin Le Clear: No 4th World Connection at all. 1st Issue Special was where they tried out new series ideas. Kirby had done the original Mahunter (Paul Kirk) strip back in the 40’s for us with Joe Simon. The 1st issue Special story took the old strip name updated it with a new character/version named Mark Shaw with a distinctive costume that would also be used by the later versions of the Manhunters.This 1975 tryout strip and character is just called MANHUNTER. DC did not launch it as a new series – but picked up the concept  and expanded it greatly in other series starting with Justice League of America #140. But Justice League of America #140 is actually directly connected to earlier Jack Kirby story in 1st Issue Specials (I’ve wrongly thought for years that they only took the look of the Manhunters from Kirby – but  it’s Mark Shaw and his other characters appearing in JLA #140). Even though The Manhunters have morphed into an Army of Machines –  Kirby deserves credit for both the original design and concept of The Manhunters. JLA #140 expanded the concept – but is a follow-up issue to Kirby.
